svg.title: Rubi: PS Vita in-game controls
svg.desc: The Vita display is an illustrated preview of Rubi over a visual novel scene. Default controls: L plus R opens or closes Rubi. Select plus R toggles the subtitle strip. D-pad left and right move by matched word, or by character in Character mode. Up and Down move between text rows; Up at the top opens earlier dialogue in Automatic reading mode, and Down past the last row of an earlier line moves toward the live text. The left stick moves by character horizontally and by text row vertically, stopping at the current text's ends. The right stick scrolls definitions. Tap a recognized character on the front touchscreen to look up its word. Triangle toggles reading statistics and the hook or OCR text source. Square opens the dialogue-region editor; hold Square for one second to restore the full screen. Enter saves the selected Anki card when Card mining is on. Cancel draws a box that Rubi reads once with OCR as soon as it is drawn, without saving it, for text the hook or the dialogue region misses; L plus R closes Rubi. Enter and Cancel follow the Vita's system setting: usually cross and circle respectively, but they can be swapped. PS closes Rubi and opens LiveArea. Double-tap the rear touchpad while Rubi is open for one full-screen OCR scan without changing the saved region. In the region editor, move with the left stick or D-pad, press Enter at the first corner, move to the opposite corner and press Enter to save; alternatively drag on the front screen, then press Enter. Cancel undoes the first corner or exits the editor. Hold L while launching a game to skip Rubi for that launch. The opening and subtitle shortcuts can be remapped in config.ini.
svg.metadata: Control mappings checked against docs/guide.md, core/config.c, core/buttons.h, core/region_select.c, shell/overlay.cpp and kernel/input.c at 3d415cdc plus the one-off box (Cancel). Device artwork: "PlayStation Vita illustration.svg" by Tokyoship, Wikimedia Commons (https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PlayStation_Vita_illustration.svg), licensed CC BY 3.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/). Source SVG: https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/3/3f/PlayStation_Vita_illustration.svg; SHA-256: 583f4c9b852d728d277708a01dba7ef972ba00299ff1b685d3c0631eedddbe97. Adaptations: scaled and embedded inline, IDs prefixed and editor metadata removed, illustrated Rubi overlay and control annotations added. Screen: original mock visual novel artwork from docs/promo/assets/vn/shot-s1-m2.jpg (CC0; provenance in docs/promo/README.md and docs/promo/assets/SOURCES.md), embedded unchanged, SHA-256: 8088ef7224a9c853e1b4cc7d63bb2c54b1737a495c166a92bf6eac37e6eaf73d. Overlay layout, opacity and colours follow shell/overlay.cpp, shell/rco/vitajpoverlay.xml and core/styled.h at ad16c618; sample lookup from docs/promo/src/overlay-states.json (s1-m2-ov01-open), current footer from shell/overlay.cpp (the one-off box's). Font line heights are estimates, not console measurements; the screen is an illustrated preview, not a console capture. All graphics and the JPEG are inline; no external images, fonts or scripts are required.
svg.text: Read a line. Look up a word. Make it yours.

to look up the word there.
Or drag on the touchscreen, then press Enter* to save.
Cancel*: undo corner / exit. Hold Square 1 s: restore full screen.
Saved per game. Minimum box: 32 × 32 pixels.

g.aria-label: Read text outside the dialogue box once: a box with Cancel, or the whole screen with a rear double tap
g.text: Read it once with OCR while Rubi is open.
Lift your finger (or press Enter*) and it is read.
Menus and other text, all at once.
Nothing is saved: your dialogue region stays.
Close Rubi to return to it. Minimum box: 32 × 32 pixels.
Shown here: × = Enter, ○ = Cancel. Japanese or swapped layouts
reverse them. Anki saving in the overlay needs Card mining ON.
Change the open / subtitle triggers in config.ini:
L+R · Select · Start · Select+L · Select+R · rear double-tap
Opened by rear double-tap? It scans while open; Cancel closes.
